```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(DataExplorer)
library(stringdist)

```

```{r}
data = read.csv("claims_history_2023_2026.csv", header = TRUE)
dim(data)
str(data)
summary(data)

data = data %>%
  mutate(
    VehValue = as.numeric(VehValue),
    RiskZone = as.factor(RiskZone),
    AnnualKms = as.factor(AnnualKms),
    PaymentFrequency = as.factor(PaymentFrequency),
    MultiPolicyFlag = as.logical(MultiPolicyFlag),
    Exposure = as.numeric(Exposure)
  )

str(data)
```

```{r}
data %>% summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))))
data %>% summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.))))
```

```{r}
introduce(data)
plot_intro(data)
plot_missing(data)

#create_report(data)
# Data issues

# The report also shows a huge mess in the naming meaning that if the factors remained then it would lead to unwanted dimensions. 
# e.g. "suv" and "Suv" being seperate categories
# I would want to reimport the data and string match first, specify the levels and string match.

VehicleTypes      <- c("Sedan", "SUV", "Hatch", "Ute", "Sports")
GaragingLocations <- c("Garage", "Street", "Carport", NA)
VehicleUses       <- c("Private", "Private_Business")

# 2. Match incoming data to the closest allowed value
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    VehicleType = as.factor(VehicleTypes[
      amatch(str_to_lower(VehicleType), str_to_lower(VehicleTypes), maxDist = 3)
    ]),
    
    GaragingLocation = as.factor(GaragingLocations[
      amatch(str_to_lower(GaragingLocation), str_to_lower(GaragingLocations), maxDist = 3)
    ]),
    
    VehicleUse = as.factor(VehicleUses[
      amatch(str_to_lower(VehicleUse), str_to_lower(VehicleUses), maxDist = 3)
    ])
  )

# create_report(data)


# When deciding to model the ExcessChosen as a factor I noticed that there was 4 unique values 500, 750, 999 and 1000
# To me 999 sounded odd as it was very close to 1000. Plotting the histogram I see that 999 represents a small part of the dataset 0.4%
# It could be a mistaken value, I found that occasionally on legacy insurance datasets 999 is a common value to represent 1000 as it fits
# within 3 digit field limit. Our dataset is now powerful enough to handle 4 digits. Reducing to 3 factors will also improve model stability.

histogram(data$ExcessChosen)
sum(data$ExcessChosen == 999)

# Issues with the driver age some are NA and some are -1
unique(data$DriverAge)
sum(data$DriverAge == -1)

# Following this pattern I also found issues with:
# - Driver age (we found before) -1 and NA values -> Convert -1 into NA
# - VehicleAge (VehAge) has many impossible negative values -> Check what is going on here

for (col in names(data)) {
  cat("Column:", col, "\n")
  print(unique(data[[col]]))
  cat("-----------------\n")
}

histogram(data$VehAge[data$VehAge < 0]) # seems like a small value we will first convert to NAs and assess overall missingness

# I also noticed that the driver age shows some data points at a crazy age which I don't think is possible
length(data$DriverAge[data$DriverAge > 100]) # 111 all all 150 which seems like an error
unique(data$DriverAge)

data = data %>%
  mutate(
    ExcessChosen = as.integer(if_else(ExcessChosen == 999, 1000, ExcessChosen)),
    DriverAge = if_else(DriverAge == -1, NA, DriverAge),
    VehAge = if_else(VehAge < 0, NA, VehAge)
  ) %>%
  filter(DriverAge < 120) # set max age at 120

#create_report(data)

missing = data |> filter(if_any(everything(), is.na)) # 4207 rows or 5.64% of the data is missing

# Missing values seem to not show any pattern in predicting the claim
data %>%
  mutate(is_missing = if_else(
    if_any(everything(), is.na),
    TRUE,
    FALSE
  )) %>%
  group_by(is_missing) %>%
  summarise(mean_claim = mean(ClaimAmount, na.rm = TRUE))

# Then we can remove/clean out the missing rows
data = na.omit(data)

# create_report(data)
# str(data)

duplicates = get_dupes(data) # there are 688 duplicate values

data = unique(data)

# save clean dataset
# write_csv(data, "cleaned_claims.csv")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# EDA - Motor Insurance Claims
# Dataset: cleaned_claims
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(corrplot)

claims <- cleaned_claims


# ============================================================
# 1. Basic overview
# ============================================================

dim(claims)
str(claims)
summary(claims)

# Number of unique policies
n_distinct(claims$PolicyID)

# Overall claims experience
claims %>%
  summarise(
    Observations = n(),
    TotalClaims = sum(ClaimNb),
    TotalClaimCost = sum(ClaimAmount),
    ClaimFrequency = mean(ClaimNb),
    ClaimRate = mean(ClaimNb > 0),
    AverageClaimCost = sum(ClaimAmount) / sum(ClaimNb),
    PurePremium = mean(ClaimAmount)
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. Distribution of numerical variables
# ============================================================

# Driver age
ggplot(claims, aes(x = DriverAge)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Driver Age",
    x = "Driver Age",
    y = "Number of Policies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(claims, aes(x = DriverAge)) +
  geom_density(colour = "pink") +
  geom_histogram(bin_width = 1, fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Driver Age Distribution", x = "Driver Age", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
# Years licensed
ggplot(claims, aes(x = YearsLicensed)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Years Licensed",
    x = "Years Licensed",
    y = "Number of Policies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Vehicle age
# Distribution of vehicle age

vehicle_age_counts <- claims %>%
  count(VehAge) %>%
  arrange(VehAge)

ggplot(vehicle_age_counts, aes(x = VehAge, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(
      min(vehicle_age_counts$VehAge),
      max(vehicle_age_counts$VehAge),
      by = 1
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Vehicle Age",
    x = "Vehicle Age (years)",
    y = "Number of Policies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Vehicle value
ggplot(claims, aes(x = VehValue)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Vehicle Value",
    x = "Vehicle Value ($)",
    y = "Number of Policies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Density
ggplot(claims, aes(x = Density)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Population Density",
    x = "Density (people/km²)",
    y = "Number of Policies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# 3. Distribution of categorical variables

# ============================================================
```

```{r}
#DriverAge
# ============================================================
# DRIVER AGE - CLAIM FREQUENCY EDA
# ============================================================

# 1. Average Claim Frequency by Driver Age
cleaned_claims %>%
  group_by(DriverAge) %>%
  summarise(
    AverageFrequency = mean(ClaimNb, na.rm = TRUE),
    NumberOfPolicies = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = DriverAge, y = AverageFrequency)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Claim Frequency by Driver Age",
    x = "Driver Age",
    y = "Average Claim Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# 2. Average Claim Frequency by Driver Age Group
cleaned_claims %>%
  mutate(
    AgeGroup = cut(
      DriverAge,
      breaks = c(17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 120),
      labels = c(
        "18-25", "26-35", "36-45", "46-55",
        "56-65", "66-75", "76+"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(AgeGroup) %>%
  summarise(
    AverageFrequency = mean(ClaimNb, na.rm = TRUE),
    NumberOfPolicies = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AgeGroup, y = AverageFrequency, fill = AgeGroup)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Average Claim Frequency by Driver Age Group",
    x = "Driver Age Group",
    y = "Average Claim Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# 3. Percentage of Policies with at Least One Claim by Age Group
cleaned_claims %>%
  mutate(
    AgeGroup = cut(
      DriverAge,
      breaks = c(17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 120),
      labels = c(
        "18-25", "26-35", "36-45", "46-55",
        "56-65", "66-75", "76+"
      )
    ),
    HasClaim = ClaimNb > 0
  ) %>%
  group_by(AgeGroup) %>%
  summarise(
    ClaimRate = mean(HasClaim, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AgeGroup, y = ClaimRate, fill = AgeGroup)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Policies with a Claim by Driver Age",
    x = "Driver Age Group",
    y = "Policies with a Claim (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
    Maximum = round(max(ClaimAmount), 2)
  )

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 3. Compare Poisson, Negative Binomial and ZINB models
# ============================================================
install.packages("MASS")
install.packages("pscl")
library(MASS)
library(pscl)
library(MASS)

# Check the variables in your dataset
names(cleaned_claims)

# Frequency model formula
freq_formula <- ClaimNb ~ DriverAge + YearsLicensed + VehAge + VehValue +
  VehicleType + RiskZone + Density + AnnualKms +
  ExcessChosen + GaragingLocation + VehicleUse +
  NCDLevel + TenureYears + MultiPolicyFlag +
  PaymentFrequency

# Poisson model
poisson_model <- glm(
  freq_formula,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = cleaned_claims
)

# Poisson dispersion
poisson_deviance_dispersion <- deviance(poisson_model) /
  df.residual(poisson_model)

poisson_pearson_dispersion <- sum(
  residuals(poisson_model, type = "pearson")^2
) / df.residual(poisson_model)

cat("Poisson deviance dispersion:",
    poisson_deviance_dispersion, "\n")

cat("Poisson Pearson dispersion:",
    poisson_pearson_dispersion, "\n")

# Negative Binomial model
nb_model <- glm.nb(
  freq_formula,
  data = cleaned_claims
)

cat("Negative Binomial theta:",
    nb_model$theta, "\n")

# Compare AIC
AIC(poisson_model, nb_model)

# Likelihood ratio test
anova(poisson_model, nb_model, test = "Chisq")
```

```{r}
#Out of Sample Validation
# ============================================================
# OUT-OF-SAMPLE VALIDATION: 2023-2025 TRAIN, 2026 TEST
# ============================================================

library(MASS)
library(tidyverse)
# Training and validation data
train <- cleaned_claims %>%
  filter(Year <= 2025)

test <- cleaned_claims %>%
  filter(Year == 2026)

# Same frequency formula
freq_formula <- ClaimNb ~ DriverAge + YearsLicensed + VehAge + VehValue +
  VehicleType + RiskZone + Density + AnnualKms +
  ExcessChosen + GaragingLocation + VehicleUse +
  NCDLevel + TenureYears + MultiPolicyFlag +
  PaymentFrequency

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit Poisson on training data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

poisson_train <- glm(
  freq_formula,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = train
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit Negative Binomial on training data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nb_train <- glm.nb(
  freq_formula,
  data = train
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Predictions on 2026
# ------------------------------------------------------------

test$PoissonPred <- predict(
  poisson_train,
  newdata = test,
  type = "response"
)

test$NBPred <- predict(
  nb_train,
  newdata = test,
  type = "response"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate validation metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

poisson_mae <- mean(
  abs(test$ClaimNb - test$PoissonPred)
)

nb_mae <- mean(
  abs(test$ClaimNb - test$NBPred)
)

poisson_rmse <- sqrt(
  mean((test$ClaimNb - test$PoissonPred)^2)
)

nb_rmse <- sqrt(
  mean((test$ClaimNb - test$NBPred)^2)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Aggregate predicted vs actual claims
# ------------------------------------------------------------

validation_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Poisson", "Negative Binomial"),
  MAE = c(poisson_mae, nb_mae),
  RMSE = c(poisson_rmse, nb_rmse),
  ActualClaims = sum(test$ClaimNb),
  PredictedClaims = c(
    sum(test$PoissonPred),
    sum(test$NBPred)
  ),
  ActualFrequency = mean(test$ClaimNb),
  PredictedFrequency = c(
    mean(test$PoissonPred),
    mean(test$NBPred)
  )
)

print(validation_results)
```

```{r}
#Severity Model Selection
# ============================================================
# 1. Prepare positive claim severity data
# ============================================================

severity_data <- cleaned_claims %>%
  filter(ClaimAmount > 0)

# Train: 2023-2025
severity_train <- severity_data %>%
  filter(Year <= 2025)

# Test: 2026
severity_test <- severity_data %>%
  filter(Year == 2026)


# ============================================================
# 2. Severity model formula
# ============================================================

severity_formula <- ClaimAmount ~ DriverAge + YearsLicensed + VehAge + VehValue +
  VehicleType + RiskZone + Density + AnnualKms +
  ExcessChosen + GaragingLocation + VehicleUse +
  NCDLevel + TenureYears + MultiPolicyFlag +
  PaymentFrequency


# ============================================================
# 3. Fit Gamma GLM
# ============================================================

gamma_model <- glm(
  severity_formula,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = severity_train
)


# ============================================================
# 4. Fit Lognormal model
# ============================================================
# Lognormal is fitted by modelling log(ClaimAmount)

lognormal_model <- lm(
  log(ClaimAmount) ~ DriverAge + YearsLicensed + VehAge + VehValue +
    VehicleType + RiskZone + Density + AnnualKms +
    ExcessChosen + GaragingLocation + VehicleUse +
    NCDLevel + TenureYears + MultiPolicyFlag +
    PaymentFrequency,
  data = severity_train
)


# ============================================================
# 5. Fit Inverse Gaussian GLM
# ============================================================
install.packages("statmod")
library(statmod)

inverse_gaussian_model <- glm(
  severity_formula,
  family = inverse.gaussian(link = "log"),
  data = severity_train
)


# ============================================================
# 6. AIC and BIC comparison
# ============================================================

model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Gamma",
    "Lognormal",
    "Inverse Gaussian"
  ),
  
  AIC = c(
    AIC(gamma_model),
    AIC(lognormal_model),
    AIC(inverse_gaussian_model)
  ),
  
  BIC = c(
    BIC(gamma_model),
    BIC(lognormal_model),
    BIC(inverse_gaussian_model)
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 7. Generate predictions for 2026
# ============================================================

# Gamma
gamma_pred <- predict(
  gamma_model,
  newdata = severity_test,
  type = "response"
)

# Inverse Gaussian
inverse_gaussian_pred <- predict(
  inverse_gaussian_model,
  newdata = severity_test,
  type = "response"
)

# Lognormal
# Need to transform predictions back from log scale.
# The correction factor accounts for the variance of the
# lognormal error.

lognormal_pred_log <- predict(
  lognormal_model,
  newdata = severity_test
)

lognormal_sigma2 <- summary(lognormal_model)$sigma^2

lognormal_pred <- exp(
  lognormal_pred_log + lognormal_sigma2 / 2
)


# ============================================================
# 8. Calculate MAE and RMSE
# ============================================================

actual <- severity_test$ClaimAmount

MAE <- function(actual, predicted) {
  mean(abs(actual - predicted))
}

RMSE <- function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
}


# ============================================================
# 9. Add validation results to comparison table
# ============================================================

model_comparison$MAE <- c(
  MAE(actual, gamma_pred),
  MAE(actual, lognormal_pred),
  MAE(actual, inverse_gaussian_pred)
)

model_comparison$RMSE <- c(
  RMSE(actual, gamma_pred),
  RMSE(actual, lognormal_pred),
  RMSE(actual, inverse_gaussian_pred)
)


# ============================================================
# 10. Sort by RMSE
# ============================================================

model_comparison <- model_comparison %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

print(model_comparison)


# ============================================================
# 11. Optional: view the individual model summaries
# ============================================================

summary(gamma_model)
summary(lognormal_model)
summary(inverse_gaussian_model)

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# CLAIM SEVERITY EDA

library(tidyverse)

# Only include policies with at least one claim
severity_data <- cleaned_claims %>%
  filter(
    ClaimNb > 0,
    !is.na(ClaimAmount),
    ClaimAmount >= 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ClaimSeverity = ClaimAmount / ClaimNb
  )

  filter(!is.na(DriverAge)) %>%
  mutate(AgeBand = ntile(DriverAge, 10)) %>%
  group_by(AgeBand) %>%

    title = "Average Claim Severity by Driver Age",

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Years Licensed
# ------------------------------------------------------------

severity_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(YearsLicensed)) %>%
  mutate(LicensedBand = ntile(YearsLicensed, 10)) %>%
```

```{r}
# 2027 model includes PaymentFrequency.
factors27 <- c(

  "log(VehValue)", "VehicleType", "RiskZone",
  "log1p(Density)", "AnnualKms",
  "ExcessChosen", "GaragingLocation",

  "MultiPolicyFlag", "PaymentFrequency"

factors28 <- setdiff(
  factors27,
  "PaymentFrequency"

# 5. MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION ---------------------------------

# 5. MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION ---------------------------------

fit_models <- function(data, factors) {

  data <- droplevels(data)

  rhs <- paste(
    c(factors, "YearTrend"),
    collapse = " + "
  )

  freq_formula <- as.formula(
    paste(
      "ClaimNb ~", rhs,
      "+ offset(log(Exposure))"
    )
  )

  sev_formula <- as.formula(
    paste("AvgSeverity ~", rhs)
  )

  # Frequency model
  freq <- glm(
    freq_formula,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = data
  )

  # Severity training data
  severity_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      ClaimNb > 0,
      ClaimAmount > 0
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      AvgSeverity = ClaimAmount / ClaimNb
    )

  # Remove unused levels from the DATA FRAME
  severity_data <- droplevels(severity_data)

  # Identify actual factor columns used in the model
  actual_factor_vars <- intersect(
    factor_vars,
    names(severity_data)
  )

  # Check for factors with fewer than two observed levels
  bad_factors <- actual_factor_vars[
    sapply(actual_factor_vars, function(v) {
      is.factor(severity_data[[v]]) &&
        nlevels(severity_data[[v]]) < 2
    })
  ]

  if (length(bad_factors) > 0) {
    stop(paste(
      "Severity model has factor(s) with fewer than two levels:",
      paste(bad_factors, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }

  # Fit severity model
  sev <- glm(
    sev_formula,
    family = Gamma(link = "log"),
    weights = ClaimNb,
    data = severity_data
  )

  list(
    freq = freq,
    sev = sev
  )
}


# 6. SPLIT DATA FOR VALIDATION ------------------------------

train <- book26 %>%
  filter(Year <= 2025)

test <- book26 %>%

  train,

)

summary(models_train$freq)
summary(models_train$sev)


# 7. PREDICTION FUNCTION ------------------------------------

predict_technical <- function(models, data, year) {

  newdata <- data

  # Annual policy exposure for pricing.
  newdata$Exposure <- 1

  # Set target-year trend.
  newdata$YearTrend <- year - 2026

  # Align factor levels with those used during training.
  for (v in names(models$freq$xlevels)) {

    if (v %in% names(newdata)) {

      unseen <- !is.na(newdata[[v]]) &
        !as.character(newdata[[v]]) %in%
        models$freq$xlevels[[v]]

      if (any(unseen)) {
        stop(paste(
          "Unseen category in prediction variable:",
          v,
          ". Handle this category before predicting."
        ))
      }

      newdata[[v]] <- factor(
        newdata[[v]],
        levels = models$freq$xlevels[[v]]
      )
    }
  }

  # Check missing values in variables required for prediction.
  freq_vars <- all.vars(
    delete.response(terms(models$freq))
  )

  sev_vars <- all.vars(
    delete.response(terms(models$sev))
  )

  needed_vars <- union(freq_vars, sev_vars)
  needed_vars <- intersect(needed_vars, names(newdata))

  if (anyNA(newdata[, needed_vars, drop = FALSE])) {
    stop(
      "Missing values or unseen factor levels remain in prediction data."
    )
  }

  frequency <- predict(
    models$freq,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "response"
  )

  severity <- predict(
    models$sev,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "response"
  )

  data.frame(
    ExpectedFrequency = as.numeric(frequency),
    ExpectedSeverity = as.numeric(severity),
    TechnicalPrice = as.numeric(
      frequency * severity
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}

# ============================================================
# TASK 2: COMMERCIAL PRICING AND TASK 2A PROMISE TESTING
# Run after the Task 1 code has created models27,
# book27 and predict_technical().
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)

# 1. BUSINESS ASSUMPTIONS ------------------------------------

fixed_cost <- 85
variable_expense_rate <- 0.10
profit_margin <- 0.08

ncd_schedule <- c(
  "0" = 0.00,
  "1" = 0.10,
  "2" = 0.20,
  "3" = 0.30,
  "4" = 0.40,
  "5" = 0.50,
  "6" = 0.60
)

collar <- 0.10
cap <- 0.15
instalment_loading <- 0.03


# 2. DISCOUNT FUNCTIONS --------------------------------------

get_NoClaimDiscount <- function(NCDLevel) {
  unname(ncd_schedule[as.character(NCDLevel)])
}

get_LoyaltyDiscount <- function(TenureYears) {
  ifelse(
    TenureYears >= 10, 0.10,
    ifelse(
      TenureYears >= 6, 0.06,
      ifelse(TenureYears >= 3, 0.03, 0)
    )
  )
}

get_MultiPolicyDiscount <- function(MultiPolicyFlag) {
  flag <- tolower(as.character(MultiPolicyFlag))
  ifelse(flag %in% c("true", "1"), 0.10, 0)
}


# 3. CALCULATE TECHNICAL BASE WITHOUT DOUBLE COUNTING -------

# Set NCD, tenure and multi-policy to their reference values
# when predicting the technical base. Other risk characteristics
# remain unchanged for each policy.

base27 <- book27

base27$NCDLevel <- 0
base27$TenureYears <- 0

base27$MultiPolicyFlag <- factor(
  "FALSE",
  levels = models27$freq$xlevels$MultiPolicyFlag
)

base_prediction <- predict_technical(
  models27,
  base27,
  2027
)

# Technical price with the three promised effects neutralised.
base27$TechnicalBase <- base_prediction$TechnicalPrice

# Apply fixed cost and variable expense/profit loading.
base27$LoadedBase <- (
  base27$TechnicalBase + fixed_cost
) / (
  1 - variable_expense_rate - profit_margin
)


# 4. APPLY CAP AND COLLAR TO PRE-DISCOUNT BASE ---------------

# Premium_2026 is the comparison point for each policy.
# Keep the pre-discount price within -10% and +15% of it.

if (!"Premium_2026" %in% names(base27)) {
  stop("Premium_2026 is missing from the 2027 renewal book.")
}

base27$BoundedBase <- ifelse(
  is.na(base27$Premium_2026),
  base27$LoadedBase,
  pmin(
    pmax(
      base27$LoadedBase,
      base27$Premium_2026 * (1 - collar)
    ),
    base27$Premium_2026 * (1 + cap)
  )
)

base27$CollarTriggered <- (
  !is.na(base27$Premium_2026) &
    base27$LoadedBase < base27$Premium_2026 * (1 - collar)
)

base27$CapTriggered <- (
  !is.na(base27$Premium_2026) &
    base27$LoadedBase > base27$Premium_2026 * (1 + cap)
)


# 5. APPLY THE PROMISED DISCOUNTS ----------------------------

base27$NCDDiscount <- get_NoClaimDiscount(
  base27$NCDLevel
)

base27$LoyaltyDiscount <- get_LoyaltyDiscount(
  base27$TenureYears
)

base27$MultiPolicyDiscount <- get_MultiPolicyDiscount(
  base27$MultiPolicyFlag
)

# Multiplicative application: each discount applies to the
# premium remaining after the previous discount.

base27$AfterNCD <- base27$BoundedBase *
  (1 - base27$NCDDiscount)

base27$AfterLoyalty <- base27$AfterNCD *
  (1 - base27$LoyaltyDiscount)

base27$AfterMultiPolicy <- base27$AfterLoyalty *
  (1 - base27$MultiPolicyDiscount)


# 6. APPLY MONTHLY INSTALMENT LOADING ------------------------

base27$FinalPremium <- ifelse(
  base27$PaymentFrequency == "Monthly",
  base27$AfterMultiPolicy * (1 + instalment_loading),
  base27$AfterMultiPolicy
)

# Save all intermediate stages for auditing.
technical27_commercial <- base27

write.csv(
  technical27_commercial,
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/technical_2027_commercial.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Average loaded base:", mean(base27$LoadedBase), "\n")
cat("Average bounded base:", mean(base27$BoundedBase), "\n")
cat("Average final premium:", mean(base27$FinalPremium), "\n")
cat("Policies hitting collar:", sum(base27$CollarTriggered), "\n")
cat("Policies hitting cap:", sum(base27$CapTriggered), "\n")


# ============================================================
# TASK 2A: SYSTEMATIC PROMISE TESTING
# ============================================================

# Test every NCD level (0-6), every tenure year (0-15),
# both multi-policy statuses, annual/monthly payment, and
# scenarios where the collar, neither bound, or cap applies.
#
# A $1,000 previous premium is used for the test scenarios.
# Raw pre-discount bases are $800, $1,000 and $1,300.

test_grid <- expand.grid(
  NCDLevel = 0:6,
  TenureYears = 0:15,
  MultiPolicyFlag = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  PaymentFrequency = c("Annual", "Monthly"),
  Scenario = c("Collar", "Neither", "Cap"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

test_grid$Premium_2026 <- 1000

test_grid$RawBase <- ifelse(
  test_grid$Scenario == "Collar", 800,
  ifelse(test_grid$Scenario == "Cap", 1300, 1000)
)

test_grid$BoundedBase <- pmin(
  pmax(
    test_grid$RawBase,
    test_grid$Premium_2026 * (1 - collar)
  ),
  test_grid$Premium_2026 * (1 + cap)
)

test_grid$NCDDiscount <- get_NoClaimDiscount(
  test_grid$NCDLevel
)

test_grid$LoyaltyDiscount <- get_LoyaltyDiscount(
  test_grid$TenureYears
)

test_grid$MultiPolicyDiscount <- get_MultiPolicyDiscount(
  test_grid$MultiPolicyFlag
)

test_grid$InstalmentFactor <- ifelse(
  test_grid$PaymentFrequency == "Monthly",
  1 + instalment_loading,
  1
)

# Price with all three discounts.
test_grid$FinalPremium <- test_grid$BoundedBase *
  (1 - test_grid$NCDDiscount) *
  (1 - test_grid$LoyaltyDiscount) *
  (1 - test_grid$MultiPolicyDiscount) *
  test_grid$InstalmentFactor

# Counterfactual prices with one discount removed at a time.
# This isolates the actual delivery of each promise.

test_grid$PriceWithoutNCD <- test_grid$BoundedBase *
  (1 - test_grid$LoyaltyDiscount) *
  (1 - test_grid$MultiPolicyDiscount) *
  test_grid$InstalmentFactor

test_grid$PriceWithoutLoyalty <- test_grid$BoundedBase *
  (1 - test_grid$NCDDiscount) *
  (1 - test_grid$MultiPolicyDiscount) *
  test_grid$InstalmentFactor

test_grid$PriceWithoutMultiPolicy <- test_grid$BoundedBase *
  (1 - test_grid$NCDDiscount) *
  (1 - test_grid$LoyaltyDiscount) *
  test_grid$InstalmentFactor

# Measure each discount against its counterfactual.
test_grid$NCDDelivered <- 1 -
  test_grid$FinalPremium / test_grid$PriceWithoutNCD

test_grid$LoyaltyDelivered <- 1 -
  test_grid$FinalPremium / test_grid$PriceWithoutLoyalty

test_grid$MultiPolicyDelivered <- 1 -
  test_grid$FinalPremium / test_grid$PriceWithoutMultiPolicy

# Compare actual delivery against promised discount.
test_grid$NCDError <- abs(
  test_grid$NCDDelivered - test_grid$NCDDiscount
)

test_grid$LoyaltyError <- abs(
  test_grid$LoyaltyDelivered - test_grid$LoyaltyDiscount
)

test_grid$MultiPolicyError <- abs(
  test_grid$MultiPolicyDelivered -
    test_grid$MultiPolicyDiscount
)

# Identify cap/collar triggers on the pre-discount base.
test_grid$CollarTriggered <- (
  test_grid$RawBase <
    test_grid$Premium_2026 * (1 - collar)
)

test_grid$CapTriggered <- (
  test_grid$RawBase >
    test_grid$Premium_2026 * (1 + cap)
)


# 7. SUMMARISE PROMISE TEST RESULTS --------------------------

promise_test_summary <- test_grid %>%
  group_by(Scenario) %>%
  summarise(
    PoliciesTested = n(),
    CollarTriggered = sum(CollarTriggered),
    CapTriggered = sum(CapTriggered),
    MaxNCDError = max(NCDError),
    MaxLoyaltyError = max(LoyaltyError),
    MaxMultiPolicyError = max(MultiPolicyError),
    AllPromisesDelivered = (
      max(NCDError) < 1e-10 &
        max(LoyaltyError) < 1e-10 &
        max(MultiPolicyError) < 1e-10
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(promise_test_summary)

# Verify every tested combination receives its full discount.
stopifnot(
  max(test_grid$NCDError) < 1e-10,
  max(test_grid$LoyaltyError) < 1e-10,
  max(test_grid$MultiPolicyError) < 1e-10
)

# Save the full systematic test and summary.
write.csv(
  test_grid,
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/task2a_promise_test_detail.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  promise_test_summary,
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/task2a_promise_test_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Task 2A systematic promise test passed.\n")

```

```{r}
#Task 2B

library(dplyr)

# 1. Restore original policy characteristics from renewal file
renewal27_original <- read.csv(
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/renewal_book_2027.csv"
)

# Restore tenure and other variables that may have been overwritten
restore_cols <- c(
  "PolicyID", "TenureYears", "NCDLevel",
  "MultiPolicyFlag", "PaymentFrequency"
)

technical27_commercial <- technical27_commercial %>%
  select(-any_of(c("TenureYears_original")))

technical27_commercial <- technical27_commercial %>%
  select(-any_of(setdiff(restore_cols, "PolicyID"))) %>%
  left_join(
    renewal27_original %>% select(all_of(restore_cols)),
    by = "PolicyID"
  )

# Standardise multi-policy flag
technical27_commercial$MultiPolicyFlag <- factor(
  ifelse(
    as.character(technical27_commercial$MultiPolicyFlag) %in%
      c("1", "TRUE"),
    "TRUE", "FALSE"
  )
)

# 2. Rebuild Task 2B data
loyalty_data <- technical27_commercial %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(TechnicalPrice),
    TechnicalPrice > 0,
    is.finite(FinalPremium),
    FinalPremium > 0,
    !is.na(TenureYears)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RelativePremium = FinalPremium / TechnicalPrice,
    TenureBand = case_when(
      TenureYears <= 2 ~ "0-2 years",
      TenureYears <= 5 ~ "3-5 years",
      TenureYears <= 9 ~ "6-9 years",
      TenureYears >= 10 ~ "10+ years"
    ),
    TenureBand = factor(
      TenureBand,
      levels = c("0-2 years", "3-5 years", "6-9 years", "10+ years")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(TenureBand)) %>%
  droplevels()

# Check tenure groups
print(table(loyalty_data$TenureBand))

# 3. Summary by tenure group
tenure_summary <- loyalty_data %>%
  group_by(TenureBand) %>%
  summarise(
    Policies = n(),
    MeanTechnicalPrice = mean(TechnicalPrice),
    MeanFinalPremium = mean(FinalPremium),
    MeanRelativePremium = mean(RelativePremium),
    MedianRelativePremium = median(RelativePremium),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(tenure_summary)

# 4. Keep only predictors with variation
categorical_vars <- c(
  "VehicleType", "RiskZone", "AnnualKms",
  "GaragingLocation", "VehicleUse",
  "MultiPolicyFlag", "PaymentFrequency"
)

categorical_vars <- categorical_vars[
  sapply(technical27_commercial[categorical_vars], function(x) {
    nlevels(droplevels(as.factor(x))) >= 2
  })
]

numeric_vars <- c(
  "DriverAge", "YearsLicensed", "VehAge",
  "VehValue", "Density", "ExcessChosen", "NCDLevel"
)

numeric_vars <- numeric_vars[
  sapply(loyalty_data[numeric_vars], function(x) {
    length(unique(na.omit(x))) >= 2
  })
]

# 5. Risk-adjusted regression
model_formula <- as.formula(
  paste(
    "log(RelativePremium) ~ TenureBand +",
    paste(c(categorical_vars, numeric_vars), collapse = " + ")
  )
)

loyalty_model <- lm(
  model_formula,
  data = loyalty_data,
  na.action = na.exclude
)

print(summary(loyalty_model))

# 6. Adjusted tenure differences
model_results <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(loyalty_model)))
model_results$Term <- rownames(model_results)
rownames(model_results) <- NULL

tenure_results <- model_results %>%
  filter(grepl("^TenureBand", Term)) %>%
  mutate(
    AdjustedDifferencePct = (exp(Estimate) - 1) * 100,
    SignificantAt5Pct = `Pr(>|t|)` < 0.05
  )

print(tenure_results)

# 7. Save outputs
write.csv(
  tenure_summary,
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/task2b_tenure_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  tenure_results,
  "C:/Users/zhcen/Downloads/task2b_risk_adjusted_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Task 2B completed.\n")
```
